new_task.label: delegate directory management access
new_task.outcome: a member who is not an Owner holds a custom role carrying the Directory or Libraries permission, so they may submit and manage directory listings
new_task.why: No taxonomy task covers granting another member permission to submit; it is a precondition of T-058, not its outcome, since nothing is filed after the last step.

records.outcome: a member other than an Owner can submit and manage directory listings through the custom role assigned to them
preconditions: Enterprise plan (Team plans do not have custom roles)
steps: Open Organization settings > Roles
Create a custom role
Give it the Directory permission for directory submissions only, or the Libraries permission for broader access
Assign that role to the member

evidence.quote: an Owner can delegate this to other members by creating a custom role in **Organization settings > Roles**

records.notes: On Team plans this stays with Owners.

records.outcome: the local connector carries the privacy policy disclosures the review requires, so it will not be rejected on that ground; nothing has been filed
steps: Add a "Privacy Policy" section to README.md
Add a privacy_policies array to manifest.json
Point the entries at HTTPS privacy policy URLs
Cover data collection, usage and storage, third-party sharing, retention, and contact information
records.notes: Missing or incomplete privacy policies result in immediate rejection.

records.outcome: carousel screenshots and their paired prompt text meet the directory asset specifications and are ready to attach to an MCP App submission
steps: Capture three to five PNG screenshots at least 1000px wide
Crop each to the app response only, leaving out the prompt
Provide the prompt text separately for each screenshot
Optionally start from the Anthropic MCP Apps Figma community carousel template

evidence.quote: **Crop:** to the app response only—**do not include the prompt** in the image

records.notes: Video and GIF are not accepted; no separate mobile assets are required. Mechanism is 'other' because the text does not say where the screenshots are produced.

records.outcome: the connector has been run against the pre-submission checklist and, for a plugin, validated, before anything is filed
steps: Run the pre-submission checklist from the review criteria page
For plugins, run claude plugin validate
Submit only after both pass

evidence.quote: for plugins, `claude plugin validate` before you submit

records.outcome: the destinations declared at submission open without the "Open external link" confirmation prompt; other destinations still prompt
preconditions: the connector uses the ui/open-link capability
every origin or scheme listed is owned by the submitting organization
steps: List with your submission every link target your server will request
Give each as an HTTPS origin such as https://example.com, listing each subdomain separately
Or give a custom URI scheme such as myapp: for deep links into a native app you own
Leave out any third-party domain or URI scheme you do not publish

evidence.quote: provide the list of link targets your server will request. Claude uses this list to suppress the "Open external link" confirmation prompt for destinations you've declared.

records.notes: The field is optional; entries you do not own are removed during review.

records.outcome: a remote MCP server, including an MCP App, has been filed through the submission portal with all seven policy acknowledgments given, and is queued for review
preconditions: directory management access: Owner, or a custom role with the Directory or Libraries permission
documentation URL, privacy policy URL, icon, and test account credentials ready
carousel screenshots if submitting an MCP App
steps: Open the submission portal in your organization's settings on Claude.ai
Read the Introduction step on what a directory listing does and does not do
In Connection, confirm the https:// server URL, the transport, and whether users reach the server by Universal URL, Multiple URLs, or a URL pattern
In Tools, let tools, prompts, and resources sync, and fix any tools flagged for missing titles or annotations on your server
In Listing, enter server name, tagline, description, one to five categories, documentation and privacy policy URLs, support contact, icon, and URL slug
In Use cases, describe the primary use cases, what users need before connecting, and whether the connector reads, writes, or both
In Company, give company name and website plus a primary contact for review updates
In Authentication, choose OAuth, a custom connection, or no authentication, within the limits your Connection choice imposes
In Data handling, state whether the API is your own, proxied with permission, or a third party's, and whether health data or sponsored content is involved
In Test & launch, give test-account setup and access instructions and confirm you have run every tool via MCP Inspector or as a custom connector in Claude
In Compliance, give all seven policy acknowledgments
Read through the Review step and submit

evidence.anchor: ### What to expect in the portal
evidence.quote: The portal walks you through the following steps. Your progress saves automatically in your browser as you move between steps

records.notes: The portal accepts remote MCP servers only; the URL slug is permanent once published.

no portal or organization access required

records.outcome: the developer has seen where the submission stands in review and read the reviewer's feedback, with an email escalation path
steps: Open the submissions dashboard at claude.ai/admin-settings/directory/submissions
Read the submission's status and any reviewer feedback
Email mcp-review@anthropic.com for escalations

evidence.quote: track your submission's status and read reviewer feedback in the [submissions dashboard](https://claude.ai/admin-settings/directory/submissions)

records.notes: Post-publication health and usage metrics are on the Managing your listing page, not here.

Left unextracted: the intro, what-you-can-submit list, directory terms, the numbered submission requirements, and the detail-card note, which state facts or requirements without actions.
